newsitem.title: CANADA: Videotron to focus on telecom services.
newsitem.headline: Videotron to focus on telecom services.

text.p: Groupe Videotron Ltd plans to focus its efforts on expanding its services in Quebec's C$5 billion telecommunications market, company officials said on Tuesday.

Claude Chagnon president and chief operating officer told the annual meeting that Videotron, a cable television operator and broadcaster, will place greater emphasis on penetrating the French-speaking Canadian province's telecommunications market, which includes telephony, and local and long-distance telephone services.
"That (market) is colossal in the face of our traditional market," Chagnon said.
In 1996, telecommunications accounted for C$15.8 million of the company's C$687 million of revenues, a 60 percent increase from C$10 million in 1995.

After the meeting, Chagnon told reporters that permission to provide local and long-distance telephone service will require the approval of the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission, a federal government regulatory agency. The CRTC is expected to issue key decisions this year on setting the terms and conditions for the Canadian cable industry's move into the local telephony market.

That would allow the cable companies to compete for the first time with Canada's big telephone concerns, including Montreal-based BCE Inc, a telecommunications holding company that is Canada's largest enterprise. In recent years, the cable companies, including Videotron, have been investing heavily in upgrading their networks to allow the more efficient transmission of voice and data signals.

Chagnon said that through its existing cable television operations in Quebec, Videotron is already billing two-thirds of the province's households, giving it an advantage over other potential telephony competitors.
"We are about the only new entrant who is not starting from zero, who does not have to begin building a whole network," Chagnon said.

Andre Chagnon, chairman, said Videotron learned much from its profitable eight-year foray into the telecommunications market in the United Kingdom. On December 17, Videotron sold its U.K. holdings to Bell Cablemedia Plc for C$825 million, making a C$500 million gain on its investment.
Videotron's U.K. holdings, which include cable and telephony services in central London, will be held jointly by Bell Cablemedia, which is a unit of BCE, and Cable and Wireless Plc.

Chagnon said Videotron's U.K. experience helped it prepare for the coming deregulation of telephony and telephone services in Canada. Given the high cost of developing new networks, it made better sense for Videotron to capitalize its U.K. investment and focus on its networks in Canada and the United States, he said.
"Given the progress we made with telecommunications in the United Kingdom, cable will be something like an accessory for us," Chagnon said.
